tech.title: Neuralink receives FDA approval for 'pivotal' brain implant trial in ALS patients
tech.summary: Neuralink has received permission from the FDA to launch a trial for its LINK brain-computer interface. The study will be open to a limited number of patients with ALS in the US. It will evaluate patients' ability to control digital devices through thought and assess the system's long-term safety and reliability. If the technology proves to be safe, the trial may allow Neuralink to apply for more advanced trials and eventually release LINK onto the market.

tech.title: SpaceX Gets Approval to Launch One Million Satellites for Orbital Data Centers
tech.summary: The FCC has granted SpaceX approval to launch a million data centers into space. Anthropic and Google have already committed to paying billions of dollars in fees to rent capacity from the network. Proponents of orbital data centers say offloading advanced computing to orbit will allow developers of AI tools to avoid the headaches they are facing on Earth. There are still numerous hurdles to overcome for SpaceX to deploy data centers in space. The FCC authorization gives SpaceX until 2033 to launch and operate the first satellite and until 2040 to launch the full constellation.

tech.title: The short age of dragon riders
tech.summary: AI models available to the public have passed a threshold in August this year. They are now stronger than most theoretical physicists at most technical tasks. Models are now able to carry out complex analytical calculations, work out lengthy proofs, and turn well-posed problems into code with minimal input. There will still be joy in discoveries even if it is not only humans that push them.

tech.title: SpaceX is not a monopoly, tech incumbents obviously lack urgency, and other Harsh Truths
tech.summary: The US space industry is generally unhealthy. The legacy industry lacks vigor. SpaceX's announced intention to gracefully sunset Falcon three years from now has induced a deep, spiraling panic among industry insiders who understand that there is no alternative. The company is uniquely positioned to put compute in space, and it has been investing heavily in this direction for more than a decade. Other tech giants have largely run out of ideas to invest for future growth. Due to this lack of vision, some have resorted to dividends and stock buybacks.

Agents' ability to do problem selection, intent, and taste is improving. This means a continuous rediscovery of what pieces require human input, and what can be fully given over, is required.

data.title: Distributed primary keys
data.summary: Reproducible benchmarks compare primary key strategies for multi-region PostgreSQL across index size, WAL overhead, and failover safety. UUIDv7 is efficient and needs no coordination. Regional sequences can collide after failover, timestamp-based IDs are vulnerable to clock rollback, and composite keys simplify replication filtering but use more storage.

data.title: How Grab built Scarlet: the AI teammate that turns a Slack message into a production data pipeline
data.summary: Grab's AI agent, Scarlet, turns Slack messages and Jira tickets into data pipeline changes, checks the resulting data against production, and opens merge requests for engineers to review. After Grab introduced reusable, team-specific instructions and automated data checks, the share of Scarlet's merge requests that engineers merged rose from about 50% in May to over 85% in September.

data.title: Backfilling Tens of Billions of Rows Next to Live Logical Replication (Part 2)
data.summary: A live PostgreSQL migration moved tens of billions of rows using parallel COPY, fixed ID ranges, and resumable checkpoints. Broken WAL archiving filled the target's disk, while subscription lag retained WAL on the source until streaming = parallel cleared the backlog. Missed updates and costly joins showed why reconciliation needs checks for both correctness and performance.

data.title: Where Agents Meet the Browser: Building a Browser-Native Agent
data.summary: LinkedIn built an internal AI agent that works across tools in employees' existing Chrome sessions, turning incident threads into tickets and documents into slide decks. It uses structured page data to cut token usage and tool-specific playbooks to improve reliability, while showing its actions and linking to evidence so users can verify the work.

data.title: Legible first: how T2 built AI on what it already owned
data.summary: T2 Tea consolidated data from 14 systems into one warehouse and built a semantic layer with 243 metrics, letting off-the-shelf AI models retrieve only the data and business rules each question needs. T2 reports spending about A$30 per seat per month and completing a channel analysis in about an hour that previously took consultants weeks.

data.title: 5 Lessons in AI Context Engineering: Why More Context Is Not Better
data.summary: Salesforce's Help Agent must work out what a customer owns and is entitled to, with lookups under 200 milliseconds at the median. More data was not the answer. The team resolves relationships, business rules, and access ahead of time into Data 360 data graphs served by one lookup. Warehouse views had taken 7 to 30 seconds for one scoring workload.

data.title: Unclean leader election: Kafka trolley problem where you always end up pulling the lever
data.summary: When no in-sync replica remains available, Kafka can sacrifice durability to restore availability by electing an out-of-sync replica, potentially losing acknowledged writes. Kafka 4.0's Eligible Leader Replicas (ELR) can avoid this trade-off in certain failure scenarios. The decision to prioritize availability over durability should be made at the topic level, based on business requirements, rather than during an outage.

data.title: Polars 2.2 Brings Out-of-Core Joins and SQL-Native Iceberg Operations
data.summary: Polars 2.2 extends its streaming engine with disk-spilling equi-joins, allowing datasets larger than available RAM to be processed without exhausting memory. SQL gains INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and COPY, alongside native Iceberg table writes and maintenance operations. A new scan_database API and over 100 performance improvements further strengthen Polars as a single-node analytical engine for production data pipelines.

data.title: Orderbook-lakehouse
data.summary: Orderbook Lakehouse is a fully local, Docker-based reference architecture for incremental market-data processing using Apache Iceberg, Apache Polaris, Spark (Scala), Redpanda Connect, and SeaweedFS. HTTP events flow through Bronze, Silver, and Gold Iceberg tables to produce order-book state and trading analytics. Iceberg snapshots enable incremental processing and idempotent recovery, while Polaris coordinates atomic metadata commits. The architecture demonstrates reliable, restartable lakehouse pipelines without managed cloud infrastructure.

data.title: Hardwood 1.1 Adds Parallel Parquet Writes, S3 Support, and ALP Encoding
data.summary: Hardwood, the lightweight, dependency-free Parquet library for the JVM, introduces parallel file writing and direct S3 uploads with multipart support. The release candidate adds ALP encoding for more compact floating-point storage, field IDs for lakehouse interoperability, and a redesigned read scheduler delivering up to 1.8× faster full scans than Hardwood 1.0. These improvements position Hardwood as a high-performance alternative for JVM applications that need direct Parquet access without Hadoop dependencies.

data.title: dbt Evals: Our First Foray into Data Agent Management
data.summary: dbt Evals is a framework that asks analytics agents the same questions across multiple runs and checks their answers with SQL tests, classifiers, or LLM judges. The goal is to catch accuracy regressions when data models or metrics change, though the initial design tests a configurable stand-in for the production agent.

data.title: Compaction Was On. It Never Ran.
data.summary: Benchmarking DuckDB-based duckgate against Athena exposed a small-file problem: DuckDB was up to 25x slower on an Iceberg table containing just 440K rows spread across thousands of tiny Parquet files. Hourly partitioning created excessive fragmentation, while AWS Glue compaction was enabled but never executed. DuckDB 2.0's asynchronous remote Parquet I/O narrowed the performance gap to roughly 4×, but the fundamental lesson remains: table layout and effective maintenance can matter more than query engine selection.

data.title: Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL
data.summary: Text-to-SQL joins that repeat an entity silently inflate SUM and COUNT, and grain-aware hints cut these fan-out errors on BIRD from 18.4% to about 13%.

data.title: Graticule: Turn Oscilloscope Screenshots Into CSV Data and Plots
data.summary: Graticule reads the grid and scales from an oscilloscope screenshot or phone photo, then exports every trace as CSV with measurements, all inside the browser.

marketing.title: Consumer trust around Black Friday deals is down
marketing.summary: Black Friday has stretched into a month of discounts, which removed the urgency that once made a 30% off banner work. Nearly three-quarters of shoppers now call the event more hype than genuine savings, even at brands whose deals match last year's. More sale days spread the same demand thinner, but brands say opting out is not an option. The ones adapting rotate individual products through deals to rebuild momentum or move the promo budget into a brand campaign instead.

marketing.title: AI is moving way too fast
marketing.summary: AI capabilities are advancing faster than society can adapt. While human expertise still plays a critical role in directing AI today, that advantage may not last as models develop stronger reasoning and research abilities. The bigger concern is that AI labs are racing toward superintelligence without clear plans to control it or align it with human interests. Political systems may struggle to keep pace with the technology's rapid evolution.

marketing.title: Behind Good Content: AEO expert Kevin White (34 minute podcast)
marketing.summary: This podcast features Kevin White sharing how brands can improve their visibility in AI search. He explains the 3 stages of AEO - being cited, mentioned, and recommended - then breaks down Scrunch's strategy for increasing its AI mention rate from 15% to 40% in 2 months. The playbook focuses on updating existing content, earning placements on trusted third-party sites, and publishing targeted FAQs. He also explains why AEO requires ongoing updates, as citations typically decay within 6-8 weeks.

marketing.title: Win Report: The three words we added to a product page that increased conversions by 12%
marketing.summary: Adding context to customer review counts can make social proof more persuasive and increase product conversions. DiamondBack Covers tested replacing an unlabeled review count with the phrase “2,863 Real-World Reviews” next to its 4.9-star rating. The change increased conversions by 12%. Research showed that 16% of skeptical buyers cited positive reviews and research as a reason they ultimately purchased. Clearly identifying reviews as real customer experiences can help reduce purchase hesitation.

marketing.title: What marketers should build next with AI
marketing.summary: This guide teaches how to become AI builders by creating custom skills and agents instead of relying on basic AI prompts. It shares 30 ideas for automating internal workflows and creating interactive tools for audiences. Examples include building brand voice checkers, customer benchmark tools, and reusable AI skills. It also explains how MCPs connect these builds to tools like Claude and ChatGPT, with a walkthrough using Lovable.

marketing.title: AI Shopping Agents Bought A Fake Deal 37% Of The Time – Claude Opus Never Did
marketing.summary: AI shopping agents often prioritize ratings and low prices over signs of fraudulent listings, creating an opportunity for misleading products to win recommendations. In a test of 9 AI models across 6,156 shopping trips, 8 models bought an obviously fake deal 37% of the time, even when they recognized suspicious pricing. Listing order also mattered: agents bought the fake 65% of the time when it appeared first, compared with 34% elsewhere. When asked to find the best value, agents chose the fake 53% of the time, suggesting that AI shopping recommendations can be vulnerable to misleading reviews, pricing, and product positioning.

marketing.title: Holidays Happen on TikTok
marketing.summary: TikTok's holiday guide on seasonal trends, creator recommendations, and shopping content. This year's emerging trends include Whimsy Christmas décor, DIY gifts, nostalgic decorations, and cozy holiday experiences. Posts about stocking stuffers are up almost 200%, while beauty advent calendar posts have grown nearly 640%, highlighting demand for smaller, giftable products. Holiday searches are also surging, including a more than 40x increase in searches for Christmas decorations and a 31x increase for Christmas lists. Brands can tap into these trends through creator partnerships, shoppable content, and timely products that reflect what consumers are already searching for and discussing.

marketing.title: How many products does an ecommerce category page need?
marketing.summary: Across 25,000+ Shopify category pages, most of the gain in Google visibility came from the first 16 products, with much smaller gains after that. The cutoff moved with search demand, since niche categories stopped improving at 9-16 products while mid-volume ones kept climbing until 33-64. Homepage links mattered more as categories grew, since linked ones ranked 15-30 points higher at every size and kept climbing after unlinked ones stalled at 9-16 products. Empty categories are better merged or redirected, since nearly half still appeared in search with nothing on the page.

marketing.title: How Black Friday Changes AI Shopping Answers
marketing.summary: Black Friday changes which pages AI shopping answers cite, not which brands they name. Publisher best-of lists grew to 65-94% of Black Friday citations in toys and superstores, with most of the gain in the final 10 days. Brand websites gained none of that share, and most of it went to pages published that season rather than older ones refreshed with the new year. On ChatGPT's product tiles, about 4 in 10 products got cheaper that week, but the most-reviewed product came first more often than the cheapest.

marketing.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse

Figma calls the claims meritless, saying it tolerates neither harassment nor extortion.

design.title: Google brings 15-second clips and scene extension to Flow with Omni 1.2
design.summary: Google has upgraded its AI filmmaking tool Flow with Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, enabling users to generate continuous video clips up to 15 seconds long. New capabilities include extending existing clips by up to 10 seconds per prompt, introducing characters or props through image references, and restaging scenes while preserving their composition. Free users receive 50 daily credits with shorter generation limits, while paid subscribers unlock longer clips, extensions, and upscaling to 1080p or 4K.

design.title: Carling's new identity is a badge of belonging inspired by its football ties
design.summary: BrandOpus has redesigned Carling's visual identity around a football-inspired crest that celebrates the lager brand's brewing heritage and longstanding connection to British football culture. The badge incorporates illustrations of the historic Carling Brewery, Burton Bridge, barley sprigs, and the signature Black Label banner. A flexible visual system of illustrations, murals, and stadium advertising adapts to individual football clubs, reinforcing Carling's positioning around community, friendship, and belonging.

design.title: TEACH: A Practical Hierarchy for Styling Design Systems
design.summary: TEACH orders design-system styling into five layers — tokens, elements, attributes, classes, and high-level components — starting with what the browser already provides. Native elements and attributes like [aria-expanded] or :user-invalid can carry much of the look and state before any custom class exists. Components sit at the top, packaging the lower layers into reusable building blocks that need considerably less custom CSS.

design.title: Craft First, AI Second
design.summary: Designers risk becoming reviewers of AI output unless they keep sketching, iterating, and defining how things should look before handing work to agents. Automating easy tasks makes the hard parts harder. A Harvard Business Review survey found 14% of AI-using workers reporting "AI brain fry." Precise prompts, saved decisions, and a personal collection of references help close the gap between taste and execution.

design.title: What UX Tasks Will AI Be Able to Do, and When?
design.summary: AI will outperform humans at every UX task with a verifiable outcome by 2030, including interface design, research, and usability evaluation. AI masters tasks in order of how easily and inexpensively their results can be verified, with UX development estimated to trail coding by approximately one year. As design execution becomes increasingly automated, human designers will focus more on identifying worthwhile problems, setting direction, aligning stakeholders, and validating outcomes with real users.

Designed to work across Co-op's food, insurance, funeral, and legal services, the identity connects its heritage with an ambition to grow membership from five million to eight million by 2030.

design.title: Interstate unveils “unapologetically British” redesign for Byron Burgers

The repositioning extends to a simplified menu inspired by British culinary traditions, supporting the company's ambition to expand from seven to 25 UK locations.

Each piece of advice was chosen to help founders think in a way they may not have thought in before.

founders.title: Framer Automations, Connectors, and Slack Agent
founders.summary: Framer sites can now run automated workflows on a schedule or on project events, like an SEO audit on publish or lead enrichment on a form submission. New connectors pull in Slack, Notion, and Ahrefs, and a @Framer Slack app handles site edits and analytics without opening the dashboard.

founders.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community (2 minute form)
founders.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join .

founders.title: Why 2027 Is the Year of USER
founders.summary: Everything that only deals with 'things' and not with 'people' is quickly losing value. AI will soon solve all tasks with verifiable rewards. They can build almost anything very easily. The new metrics that still work are how many resources you have that other people cannot get, and how much your work affects people. Both require real people to spend time or money, as nobody can generate them from nothing.

founders.title: Startups Are Picking Names That Can Work Even If The Original Business Model Doesn't
founders.summary: Recently funded startups are favoring names that are distinctive but vague, like Also, Sunday, or Flapping Airplanes, so they can pivot without a rebrand. Many companies make one or two major pivots within seven or eight years.

founders.title: The Fall Fundraising Window is Now Closed
founders.summary: Fundraising processes launched after Thanksgiving run into the December holiday break. Pushing to close before year-end for founders who already hold a signed term sheet. Founders with soft-circled angels and no lead can close those commitments now so they do not lose them. Founders without real investor traction should consider pausing to improve the business and restart in January. Casual intro calls in December can still build relationships for January.

founders.title: Amir Satvat: 184 Game Studios Have Closed Since 2022
founders.summary: Over a third of the 184 game studios closed since 2022 had raised investment or been acquired before shutting down.

founders.title: How I automated my bookkeeping with AI and replaced the work I outsourced to an admin assistant
founders.summary: Claude reads scanned receipts and renames them, and a separate agent browser downloads receipts from websites using 1Password's command-line tool.

founders.title: Build vs. Buy When Building Just Got Cheap
founders.summary: Spending engineering resources on solved problems was rarely worth it, until AI came along.

founders.summary: Most AI-native services roll-ups still pitch as if equity will fund every acquisition.

founders.title: Sales reps do not push the customer portal
founders.summary: A pest-control field note describes reps avoiding portal promotion because adoption brought no extra pay and they distrusted central support.

crypto.title: Coinbase and State Department Host Dublin DPRK Crypto Symposium
crypto.summary: Coinbase and the US State Department co-sponsored a two-day Dublin symposium on North Korean cyber threats to crypto, joined by Global Affairs Canada, Google, and Payward. FBI, FinCEN, and Ireland's Garda National Cyber Crime Bureau participated in sessions covering two DPRK threat vectors: crypto heists funneling proceeds into weapons programs and fake IT workers using false identities to secure remote positions at crypto firms. The event consolidates US, Canadian, and Irish law enforcement with major crypto and tech companies into a shared operational framework for countering state-sponsored financial crime.

crypto.title: Push to scrap SEC's Regulation Crypto and innovation exemption
crypto.summary: Senators Warren, Van Hollen, and Tina Smith, with other Banking Committee members, sent SEC Chair Atkins two letters demanding the agency withdraw its crypto offering rules and its tokenized stock "innovation exemption." The August proposal exempts crypto offerings up to $5M for four years and up to $75M for one year from registration. The five-year innovation exemption would keep tokenized securities venues from being treated as exchanges, which the senators say creates a "shadow stock market" that fragments liquidity and invites illicit finance.

crypto.title: Backpack Launches Open RFQ Marketplace for Stock Order Flow
crypto.summary: Backpack Exchange launched an RFQ system for stocks, letting any market maker submit two-sided quotes that compete with Backpack's own executing broker on each order. The system combines native Backpack liquidity with traditional finance liquidity, routing retail stock orders to whichever counterparty offers the best price at execution time. Open access means any market maker can plug in without special arrangements, increasing competitive pressure on each fill across Backpack's stock order flow. The design mirrors RFQ mechanisms common in traditional equity markets, where fragmented liquidity pools compete on price rather than posting to a single central order book.

crypto.title: OKXICE Opens 24/7 Stock Trading With Six Live Tokens
crypto.summary: OKX launched OKXICE, a tokenized stock trading platform routing six equity tokens through Uniswap v4 pools for 24/7 on-chain trading. The inaugural pools held $1.22 million in liquidity after the first day, and OKX has confirmed a rollout pipeline of 113 total assets including the current listings. The Uniswap v4 integration makes these tokens composable with existing DeFi protocols, extending tokenized equities beyond isolated wrappers into natively on-chain instruments.

crypto.title: 75+ Free Tier Crypto APIs Cataloged Across 10 Categories
crypto.summary: A developer-compiled directory at freecryptoapis.com catalogs 75+ free-tier access points across 10 categories, from swap aggregators to security tooling, giving builders a single reference for assembling zero-cost infrastructure stacks. The most generous allocations include dRPC at 50M compute units/month, Helius at 1M credits/month, Alchemy at 30M compute units/month, 1inch at 100K calls/month, and Neynar at 10M credits/month. A dozen entries require no API key at all, including Jupiter, DEX Screener, Hyperliquid, Binance, PublicNode across 77 chains, Pyth, ENS, and mempool.space. Category coverage runs deepest in RPC/node providers (12), market data (12), and swap/execution (11), with explorers (8), analytics/indexing (7), identity/social (6), and oracles (5) rounding out the set.

crypto.title: 2026 Onchain AI Portfolio Review and 2027 Reallocation Plans
crypto.summary: 0xJeff, a prominent Onchain AI sector investor, published a 2026 portfolio retrospective acknowledging mixed results across the year and sharing specific holdings, mistakes, and lessons. 2026 was a difficult period for Onchain AI token allocations, consistent with broader crypto market pressure following BTC's decline from October 2025 highs. There will be 2027 reallocation plans within the Onchain AI sector, indicating a repositioning rather than an exit from the category.

crypto.title: Aave vs Morpho: An Asset Issuer's Guide
crypto.summary: Aave V4 pools liquidity in Hubs that Spokes borrow from up to a cap, so unrecovered debt becomes a Hub deficit shared by all suppliers of that asset, while Morpho's isolated markets with five fixed parameters keep bad debt inside one market and the curator vault that funded it. Morpho holds about $11.3B in deposits against $15.8B on Aave V3, and during April's Kelp rsETH exploit, Aave lost $8.45B in deposits over 48 hours while Morpho's losses stayed in rsETH-exposed markets. Morpho's liquidation formula gives a 62.5% LLTV market such as Robinhood's NVDA a 12.7% incentive and 2.7x theoretical leverage, versus 2.6% and 11.8x at 91.5% LLTV. Recommended venues by asset: Morpho first for yield-bearing stablecoins with Aave for scale, wherever borrowers are for payment stablecoins, Horizon for credit RWAs, and the distribution partner's venue for tokenized stocks, such as Coinbase's Aave V4 Spoke and Robinhood's Morpho markets.

crypto.title: How to market tokenized assets
crypto.summary: RWA products are good, but few people outside crypto know about them because marketing speaks to crypto insiders. Lead with the problem rather than the technology, explain what being onchain adds, and market beyond Crypto Twitter through YouTube, TikTok, finance podcasts, and creators. Partnering with fintechs, neobanks, and brokers that already have users lets the blockchain stay invisible. Content should explain where yield comes from, what backs the asset, who is responsible, and what the risks are, since trust is part of the product. Tokenization is early, like cards or Apple Pay once were.

crypto.summary: Nvidia will pay $290M to settle a class action alleging it understated crypto mining's contribution to 2017 and 2018 gaming GPU sales.

crypto.summary: Agentic commerce is in its forming and storming phase, and new behavior needs incentives that are currently misaligned.

it.title: Rackspace shuts down Spot cloud platform after security breach
it.summary: Rackspace will permanently discontinue its Spot Kubernetes service on December 8 at 5 PM Central following a security breach. Customers must migrate workloads and download their data before that deadline, when remaining workloads will be terminated and stored data will become inaccessible. All Spot customers are being told to treat API tokens, kubeconfigs, and Kubernetes Secrets as potentially compromised, even if they did not receive an earlier breach notification. Rackspace says it has found no evidence that the incident extended to its core infrastructure or other customer environments.

it.title: HPE shares tumble as shrinking AI margins overshadow upbeat forecast
it.summary: HPE shares fell about 16% after lower margin expectations overshadowed an improved fiscal 2027 revenue-growth forecast of 27–35%. Fourth-quarter revenue increased 50% to $14.55 billion, helped by strong AI server demand. CFO Marie Myers said component costs are rising faster than selling prices, with further margin pressure expected as AI server shipments increase in the second half of the fiscal year.

it.title: European IT spending set for 9.9% surge in 2027 amid AI-optimized server boom
it.summary: Gartner expects European IT spending to reach $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9% from 2026. Data-center spending is forecast to reach $167.6 billion, while software spending climbs 13.3% to $385.2 billion. AI infrastructure demand and higher server prices are driving much of the increase. Gartner also expects software purchasing to shift from individual AI agents toward systems that coordinate workflows across multiple business functions.

it.title: Do legacy systems wear out?
it.summary: This post examines how maintenance and vendor support shape the reliability of aging infrastructure. Hardware components deteriorate, but replacement parts, monitoring, and redundancy can keep an older platform operating reliably. Software presents a different challenge: changing workloads, missing patches, and the end of vendor support can make a functioning system increasingly risky. Upgrade or retire software before support ends, while maintaining the skills and parts needed to operate older hardware.

it.title: I built an AI agent. It broke my assumptions about my own team
it.summary: CTO Matthew Finlayson describes building four versions of an agent to route customer issues to engineering teams. The project revealed that assignments depended on undocumented ownership rules, exceptions, and judgment that managers explained through reviewing real cases. He reports that their feedback helped improve routing accuracy from about 60% to 95%. The experience also shaped how he evaluated the project, including access to the right systems, ongoing validation, operating costs, and the amount of manual work removed.

it.title: MCP servers can now ship skills, run tasks, and more with Claude
it.summary: Anthropic has launched Skills over MCP in public beta for Claude, allowing Model Context Protocol servers to publish specific workflows and guidance alongside their tools. Additionally, the company announced that Tasks and Elicitation features are now generally available to support long-running, interactive work and user sign-offs, with File Uploads rolling out soon.

it.title: Introducing Bits Maintenance, your AI teammate for infrastructure patching and upgrades
it.summary: Datadog is introducing Bits Maintenance, an AI teammate designed to automate infrastructure patching and upgrades for open source software. Currently available in preview, the tool tracks releases and vulnerabilities, analyzes changes against environment configurations, generates tailored upgrade plans, and executes pull requests based on user-defined guardrails.

it.title: How Workday's CIO Is Preparing IT for the AI Era
it.summary: Workday CIO Rani Johnson discusses rebuilding the company's data lake, identity infrastructure, and Salesforce environment to create a stronger foundation for AI. She describes aligning IT roadmaps with business priorities and agreeing on how the value of investments will be measured. Johnson says partnering with learning and development helped raise enterprise AI adoption from below 50% to over 96% by addressing skills and behavior changes. She also argues that CIOs should actively create career opportunities for their teams as technology changes the work they perform.

it.title: Modernizing Retail Kiosks with Windows Autopilot and Microsoft Intune
it.summary: Microsoft outlines how it moved retail checkout devices from domain-joined, Configuration Manager-managed builds to Windows Autopilot and Intune. The new setup uses Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC, Microsoft Entra join, and provisioning without an individual user account. The team registered existing devices before cutover, separated pilot and production deployments, and used device certificates for Wi-Fi access. The case study also explains how the checkout application replaces the standard Windows desktop and how application servicing accommodates store operations.

it.title: Rooms "More actions" Panel Reordering
it.summary: Google Meet room-controller menus will prioritize frequently used controls, with Early Preview rollout starting December 2 and wider rollout starting December 11.

it.title: From Jira to OpenProject: A major milestone for digital sovereignty in Germany
it.summary: Germany's central federal IT provider, ITZBund, chose OpenProject as an open-source alternative to Atlassian Jira.

it.title: Inside Capital One's multi-agent system
it.summary: Capital One cut human edit rates for AI-generated customer support summaries by about 80% with its MACAW agent system.
